home.featuredSubtitle: Small-batch bars that keep leaving our shelves.
home.storyLead: It started in my kitchen. A long afternoon, a borrowed pot, and the bar of soap I wanted but couldn't buy.
home.storyBody: Twelve years later, the pot is bigger and the recipes are sharper — but the bars are still made a little at a time, poured by hand, and cured for a month before they reach you.
home.t1: "My daughter's eczema loves the unscented tallow bar. Finally, something that lasts."
home.t2: "The lavender olive is my shower treat. It smells like a holiday."
home.t3: "Bought the trio as a gift; got asked for the link five times."

about.title: About Rebecca's Natural Soaps
about.intro: Rebecca's is a one-woman soap workshop in central Israel. I started it in 2014 because the soap I wanted didn't exist — gentle enough for my daughter, honest enough for me.
about.ingredients: We work with three ingredient families: grass-fed tallow, extra-virgin olive oil, and plant-only bases for our vegan range. Each family has its own feel on the skin, and its own small rituals in the kitchen.
about.process: Every bar is cold-processed and cured for at least four weeks. That slow cure is what makes the lather creamy and the soap long-lasting — there are no shortcuts for it, and we're not interested in faking one.
about.values: No synthetic fragrance, no parabens, no palm oil. Packaging is paper and string. When we make mistakes, we own them; when we change a recipe, we tell you why.
about.closing: If you'd like to talk, try the contact page. I read every message myself. — Rebecca
